source.title: Why does weak-OOD help? A Further Step Towards Understanding Jailbreaking VLMs
source.authors: Yuxuan Zhou; Yu-Zhao Peng; Yang Bai; Kuo-Feng Gao; Yi-Hao Zhang; Ye-Chao Zhang; Xun Chen; Tao Yu; Tao Dai; Shu-Tao Xia

record.file_problem: Minor OCR/figure-extraction corruption in parts of the appendix; the main text and relevant tables are readable.
record.tranche_reason: The study tests whether intent-related understanding and refusal respond differently to OOD changes, using behavioral probes and proxy scores rather than finding or intervening on a difference-in-means refusal direction.
record.gate_note: The paper cites the single-direction finding as background but does not extract, ablate, add, or weight-edit that direction. Its OOD attack results are not evidence that attacks suppress that specific direction. The included judge prompt is study material, not an instruction addressed to an AI reviewing this paper.
record.test_reason: In a new setting (VLMs under visual OOD shuffling), the study measures harmful-intent judgment and refusal rate separately on GPT-4o-mini and GPT-5. Judgment stays near baseline while refusal falls. This is a behavioural test bearing on V5. It never extracts, ablates or adds a difference-in-means refusal direction, so V1–V4 and V6–V8 are untested.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors conclude that mild OOD perturbations reduce refusal before intent perception degrades, giving an inverted-U in attack success. They call the pretraining/alignment robustness gap an evidence-consistent interpretation, not a demonstrated cause. They present JOCR as a practical OCR-readable attack that exploits the effect.
record.recipe_differences: The original method finds a harmful-minus-harmless activation direction and causally ablates or adds it. This study instead measures behavioral probes and proxy similarities during visual OOD perturbations; it does not find or intervene on a refusal direction.
record.method_sensitivity: Perturbation strength changes the balance: mild shifts tend to reduce refusal while retaining intent measures; stronger shifts degrade intent measures too. Outcomes also vary by model and attack setting.

fits_no_version.finding: Under mild shuffling and the JOCR perturbation, the representation similarity of the final input token to the clean input stays high. Meanwhile a logit-lens refusal-token score and the refusal rate drop sharply in Qwen2.5-VL-7B (for example, refusal 58.52 to 36.07 at intent score .2504 to .2531).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Mild visual OOD shifts move VLM activations away from the refusal-triggering region while preserving overall input representation.

record.problems: The intent/refusal latent scores are proxies, not causal interventions on an identified direction. Closed-source models are tested behaviorally rather than through internal states. The authors also note reliance on automatic judges and describe the defense study as a preliminary single-model pilot.
record.rows_left_out: No rows omitted under the 60-row limit. OOD attack-success comparisons, JOCR baseline comparisons, and safety-augmentation defense outcomes are not included because they do not measure the specific separate-encoding claim tested here or the single refusal direction.

untested.parts: No difference-in-means direction is extracted, ablated or added; no capability check.
OOD attacks lower a logit-lens refusal-token score and shift PCA position, but no test checks suppression of the refusal direction or adversarial training against its ablation.
No comparison of one direction against multiple directions or a cone.
No internal harmfulness direction versus refusal direction, and no causal intervention. The evidence is behavioural, on closed models only.
Safety fine-tuning on weak-OOD inputs is a defense test only; it does not ask whether a removable direction exists.

record.verdict_notes: The paper cites Arditi et al. and Zhao et al. (2025a) as motivation but uses no refusal direction. Harm-judgment accuracies are low even unshuffled (38.8% GPT-4o-mini, 5.6% GPT-5), which suggests the binary classification probe is partly suppressed by refusal; this weakens all V5 readings. The study does report its own text-intent probe, but no internal harmfulness measure exists for the closed models.

versions.untested_parts: No difference-in-means direction is found or causally ablated/added; other abilities are not evaluated under such an intervention.
No refusal-direction ablation is converted into a weight edit.
The study does not test whether attacks suppress the single direction or whether training against its ablation increases robustness.
No comparison of a single direction with an affine subspace, cone, or additional refusal directions.
The study uses behavioral probes and proxy scores; it does not establish separate causal representations or directly test the encoding with interventions.
JOCR's transfer to other models is not a test of transfer of the refusal direction across languages, model variants, or base-to-instruct stages.
Safety augmentation is evaluated as a defense, but the study does not test whether training timing or method determines whether one removable refusal direction exists.
No reasoning-model test of the single-direction claim.

labels.label: supports
labels.condition: GPT-4o-mini, SI-attack shuffling S-4 to S-25, behavioural probes on MM-SafetyBench
labels.reason: Harm accuracy moves 38.80->34.02 to 37.87 while refusal falls 84.11->63.08. The two respond differently, most clearly at S-4/S-9. This is behavioural evidence only, on a closed model, so it bears on V5's encoding claim only indirectly.

relation.reason: Its own Table 1 probes measure harm-judgment accuracy and refusal rate separately under graded perturbation, which bears on V5.

tranche.reason: New setting (VLMs under visual OOD shuffling) with a behavioural result on whether harm judgment and refusal respond separately; no difference-in-means direction. T2 would also be defensible.

source_check.notes: The GPT-5 probe (same protocol, Table 1) has no V5 verdict. Its harm accuracy rises from 5.61 to 21.64 at S-4 while refusal falls 97.74->91.10, and the test_reason's 'judgment stays near baseline' is wrong for GPT-5. Unshuffled harm accuracy is low (38.80, 5.61), the text gives no explanation, and no per-sample judgment-compliance link is reported, so treat the result as aggregate trends. Qwen2.5-VL-7B internal proxies (Figs 3-4) are unrecorded and may bear on V5/V3 as non-direction evidence. The call's uncertainty=y comes only from the Wilson CIs on JOCR ASR.

statements.correction: GPT-4o-mini, full MM-SafetyBench: harm accuracy (5 trials) 38.80/37.64/37.87/35.85/34.02 and refusal rate (10 trials) 84.11/73.52/67.98/65.52/63.08 at Unsh./S-4/S-9/S-16/S-25. These are aggregate rates with no per-sample joint and no uncertainty reported. Authors: intent metrics decline clearly only at stronger shuffling. GPT-5, same protocol: harm accuracy 5.61->21.64/17.44/16.76/15.54; refusal 97.74->91.10/90.36/86.00/85.23.
statements.problem: All GPT-4o-mini numbers match Table 1. Three problems. (1) 'Stated harm judgment holds while it complies' overreads aggregate trends: the text reports no per-sample link between judging harmful and complying, and harm accuracy is only 38.80% even unshuffled, below the 84.11% refusal rate. (2) 'Has uncertainty' does not hold for this result: Table 1 gives no CI or SD, and the study's Wilson CIs cover only JOCR ASR. (3) It omits the GPT-5 replication under the same protocol.

statements.correction: GPT-5 (gpt-5-2025-08-07) is also probed behaviourally, size not stated.
statements.problem: none for this study; GPT-4o-mini's size is not stated and its result is behavioural only

statements.correction: Qwen2.5-VL-7B-Instruct, 100 refused MM-SafetyBench inputs under SI-attack: layer-averaged intent score (cosine of clean vs shuffled final-token states) and refusal score (logit-lens cosine to a 50-token refusal vocabulary); PCA of layers 17/19/21 (Figs 2-4). Intent stays comparatively stable at mild shuffle while the refusal score drops in middle-to-late layers. These are proxies, not difference-in-means harm/refusal directions. LLaVA-v1.5 variants are also evaluated, with judge-derived scores only.
statements.problem: Right that no harm or refusal direction is extracted. Wrong that the study is behavioural only and on closed models only: it also measures internal proxies on the open Qwen2.5-VL-7B-Instruct.
